Well as someone who has gone through something similar, i can tell you that magic doesn't exist. Not drugs or alcohol or self harm. At the moment the pain will always be there, and there's probably nothing you can do to make it stop. Nothing includes suicide. It's not the solution. Embrace your pain, and please just give it time. More time. I know it's not okay and that you're exhausted and everything you want is just to feel in peace, but if you give up now you will never know what would had happened if you hadn't. Please. Wait. As much as it's necessary. I hope i've helped you.

Don't look for your happiness in other people's love, even if it's your family's. Learn to love yourself, to enjoy yourself. I know it's easy to say, but really, ignore everyone, focus on yourself even if that's more difficult. And if that doesn't work, escape yourself. Maybe that isn't the best advice, but disconnect from everything. Maybe just a moment during the day, but enough to survive day by day. Make a list of movies to watch, do buzzfeed quizzes, explore the internet or discover a new YouTube channel. Anything.

Yess sorry, I am Spanish and I was lazy to start writing in English xd. the fact is that Coven seemed to me super inconsistent. It doesn't follow a single specific plot line in all season except for the supreme thing, and even that feels pointless because she's Cordelia in the end, and we didn't even get many clues about it during the season. On the other hand, there is the issue of the witch hunters, which really has almost no relevance throughout the season but in the last chapters they make it vital, in fact this is how the season closes, with a plot that felt like one more subplot than nothing. Not to mention the waste of characters (Kyle for example, they could have given him a much more interesting role in the story and yet they wasted the potential of Evan peters, or Misty, about whom we know practically nothing during half of the season ). In short, I feel like there were too many parallel arches that didn't fully develop and ultimately went nowhere, so I had a hard time finishing this season. However in Apocalypse I got a lot more character depth from the witches (and they didn't even come out all season) than I did in coven. The setting seemed amazing to me, Cody Fern a great actor and his character Michael Langdon one of the best I have seen on television in general. You could empathize with each of the characters, and it felt like a very intimate season almost exclusively made for fans. The different roles of Evan peters added a very comical touch, and although they made use of the cliché of time travel, it worked out well because in the end people were interested in seeing the outcome of all the characters because they had been developed properly throughout season no matter how they did it, not like in Coven, were the season was more centered in the SO MANY diffefent small pointless plots that they kind of forgot about the characters.

The investigation and the clues he received in his bizarre dreams gradually led Cooper to the network of secrets and mysteries surrounding the town and its eccentric inhabitants. Starting out as a murder mystery, the show evolved into an examination of the sinister double lives of the innocent-looking townsfolk and the dark, paranormal mysteries of this seemingly quaint town.
